Production order

Make one finished item on a manual production order and receive it into the warehouse.

Procedure

1Confirm the existing foundation

Result
A qualified finished item, component, BOM, routing, warehouses, and stock are known.
Screen
Warehousing➔Inventory 360 (whwmd4300m000)

Why LN works this way. Nothing yet. A production order is built from master data that must already exist, and LN will not say at creation which of it is missing or wrong; it says so at release, at material issue or at completion. This task reads the finished item, its component, the BOM and routing revisions, the warehouses and the stock before the order asks for them.

StepActionYou should see
1.1Obtain one prequalified training case from the master-data ownerWrite downfinished item andcomponent item, with an existing valid BOM and routing
1.2Type the component item in the filter box above the grid's Item column and press EnterThe component's row with its inventory totals, and a row for any item whose code starts with it
1.3Tick the component's own row and click Warehouse Inventory in the Inventory groupWarehouse - Item Inventory (whwmd2515m000) opens for the component
1.4Select a warehouse row with enough unblocked stock for the quantity-one orderWrite downcomponent warehouse andcomponent on-hand before
1.5Confirm the training case names the receiving warehouse and the expected operation
1.6Confirm it names a valid BOM revision and a valid routing revisionAll inputs needed to check the created order are known before entry begins
1.7Repeat steps 1.2–1.3 for the finished item, and read the row of the receiving warehouse the training case namesWrite downfinished item on-hand before
Confirm the existing foundation: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
No qualified item/BOM/routing combination is availableStop. Production order does not create or repair master data; request a qualified training case
Warehouse Inventory opens Warehouse - Item Inventory Ownership (whwmd2615m000), Warehousing➔Inventory Reporting➔Inventory Position➔Warehouse - Item Inventory Ownership, insteadA warehouse is set in Filter Items. Clear Site and Warehouse, click Refresh, and tick the row again
Component has no suitable warehouse stockChoose another qualified case or replenish it before creating an order intended for later execution

2Create the production order

Result
A quantity-one order exists at Created status.
Screen
Manufacturing➔Job Shop➔Production Orders (tisfc0501m000)

Why LN works this way. On save LN reads the item's BOM and routing valid on the Reference Date and generates the order's operations and estimated materials from them. Quantity Ordered is what is to be produced and Warehouse is where the result will be received. The order exists at Created; nothing has moved.

StepActionYou should see
2.1Click NewA new production-order record opens
2.2Enter the finished item from step 1.1The item is accepted for the order
2.3Confirm Site for the training caseWrite downsite
2.4Enter 1 in Quantity OrderedWrite downproduction quantity = 1
2.5Confirm Warehouse is the intended receiving warehouseWrite downreceiving warehouse
2.6Confirm Production Start and Planned Delivery Date suit the training run
2.7Confirm Planning Method suits the training runThe order dates remain within the qualified BOM and routing dates
2.8If the item is revision controlled, select the qualified item revision supplied with the training caseThe selected revision is visible before save
2.9Click SaveOrder Status = CreatedWrite downproduction order number
Create the production order: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
The item or revision is rejectedStop and have the master-data owner verify the existing item and revision; do not change setup from this task
The order does not save at CreatedRecord the message and visible fields; do not substitute guessed values

3Verify the generated foundation

Result
The expected BOM, routing, operation, and estimated component are attached.
Screen
Manufacturing➔Job Shop➔Production Orders (tisfc0501m000)

Why LN works this way. The detail session shows what LN generated at creation: the planning area holds the operations from the routing and the estimated-materials area holds the components from the BOM, scaled to the order quantity. A missing operation, BOM or component here is a stop condition, not something to repair inside the order.

StepActionYou should see
3.1Double-click the production order recorded in step 2.9Production Order opens for the same order
3.2Compare the displayed BOM and revision with the qualified training caseWrite downBOM and revision match the expected foundation
3.3Compare the displayed routing and revision with the qualified training caseWrite downrouting and revision match the expected foundation
3.4Open the production-planning area and confirm the expected operation is presentWrite downexpected operation; Operations Present is selected in the overview
3.5Open the estimated-materials area and confirm the expected component and quantityWrite downestimated component quantity for the component from step 1.1
3.6Return to the overview without running a release or processing actionThe order remains Created and no material issue has begun
Verify the generated foundation: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
BOM or routing is blank or unexpectedCheck the qualified dates/revisions and record the mismatch
Validation reports a multilevel BOM loopStop. Do not improvise a replacement component or revision; the supported correction route is not yet documented
Expected operation or component is absentLeave the order at Created and return it to the master-data owner for diagnosis

4Release the order

Result
The order is Released; warehousing issue and receipt orders exist.
Screen
Manufacturing➔Job Shop➔Production Orders (tisfc0501m000)

Why LN works this way. Release changes the order to Released, the state in which production can start, and at the same moment LN creates two warehousing orders: one to issue the component out of its warehouse and one to receive the finished item into its own. Issue material to the job shop works the first; Report the operation complete and confirm warehouse receipt depends on the second.

StepActionYou should see
4.1Select the production order row from step 2.9The row is highlighted
4.2Actions➔Release OrdersRelease Production Orders (tisfc0204m000) opens
4.3Confirm the selection range narrows to this one production orderOnly this order is in scope for the release run
4.4Run the releaseThe dialog closes; back in Production Orders,Write downorder status after release = Released
4.5Confirm no other order changed statusOnly the order from step 2.9 shows Released
Release the order: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
The order does not reach ReleasedRecord the message; the release options this task does not exercise (shortages, quality, printing) may be blocking it — check them against Production Order Parameters (tisfc0100s000) before assuming a fault

5Issue material to the job shop

Result
The component is issued; the order is Active

Why LN works this way. Material issue turns the estimated quantities into an outbound warehousing order from the raw-material warehouse to the work center, and each issued quantity books a WIP transaction. That first WIP transaction is what moves the order to Active; release alone does not. How much of the outbound procedure LN runs for you depends on two check boxes on the material line.

StepActionYou should see
5.1Open Manufacturing➔Job Shop➔Production Materials➔Material to Issue for Production Orders (ticst0101m100) for the order released in Release the orderThe component line from step 1.1 is listed, with Production Order Status = Released
5.2Read Estimated Quantity and Actual Quantity for the component lineActual Quantity = 0
5.3Read To Issue by WarehouseWrite downmaterial to issue = the To Issue by Warehouse figure
5.4If the line is not already unblocked, run Initiate Inventory Issue (tisfc0207m000) for the lineThe material's warehouse order line unblocks
5.5Open Warehousing Orders (whinh2100m000) and find the production issue order for this production orderThe order shows order type 30- Production (Out), source the component warehouse from step 1.4, destination the work center from the routing
5.6Click Drill In on the issue order — Warehousing Order (whinh2100m100)The order lines and the Outbound Line Status Overview (whinh2129m000) activity list are visible
5.7If Generate Outbound Advice is unfinished and not automatic, run itThe advice is generated
5.8If Release Outbound Advice is unfinished and not automatic, run itThe advice is released
5.9Continue the outbound procedure until the issue order reaches ShippedOrdered and advised quantities match; the order shows Shipped
5.10Return to Material to Issue for Production Orders and Production OrdersActual Quantity = the estimated quantity, To Issue by Warehouse = 0;Write downorder status after material issue = Active
Issue material to the job shop: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
The material line stays blocked / To Issue by Warehouse never appearsRun Initiate Inventory Issue (tisfc0207m000) manually; if still blocked, stop and record what was observed
The issue stops short and a shortage report printsA component's stock is short and negative inventory is not allowed. The quantity waits in To Issue by Warehouse; restock, then process the warehousing order by hand
Generate/Release Outbound Advice are missing or already actionedDo not assume a fault. Direct Process Warehouse Order Line may be automatic for this material — confirm in Activities by Warehousing Order (whinh2104m000) before troubleshooting further

6Report the operation complete and confirm warehouse receipt

Result
The finished item is posted to inventory and on-hand increases at the receiving warehouse.
Screen
Manufacturing➔Job Shop➔Production Control➔Report Operations (tisfc0130m000)

Why LN works this way. Reporting the last operation complete records the quantity produced and, depending on a parameter, posts it to inventory silently, not at all, or after asking. The order becomes Production Completed when reported and Completed only when Warehousing finishes the inbound receipt, so the two statuses are a handoff, not a failure. The task ends with an inventory read because the Manufacturing-side status alone does not prove the stock arrived.

StepActionYou should see
6.1Open Manufacturing➔Job Shop➔Production Control➔Report Operations (tisfc0130m000) for the order's next operationThe operation line shows Operation Status, Planned Output, and the item from step 1.1
6.2Enter the production quantity from step 2.4 in CompletedThe quantity is accepted
6.3SaveIf this was the last operation, LN can book the completed product into inventory
6.4Repeat steps 6.1–6.3 for each remaining operation, in routing sequenceEach operation reports complete in turn
6.5If Report Orders Completed (tisfc0120s000) opens on the last operation's save, enter the completed quantity. It goes in Additional Quantity to Deliver
6.6Save the quantityLN asks "Automatically confirm receipt when activating warehouse order inbound line?" — see the note below before answering
6.7Answer the receipt question, and record which way you answeredWrite downreceipt answer;delivered = the production quantity if you answered Yes
6.8Return to Production Orders (tisfc0501m000) and read Order StatusWrite downorder status after reporting. Production Completed means Warehousing has not finished the inbound procedure yet; Completed means the goods are in inventory. On the Yes path expect Quantity Delivered = the production quantity and Quantity to Deliver = 0; on the No path the quantity sits in Quantity to Deliver until Warehousing processes the inbound line
6.9Open Inventory 360 (whwmd4300m000) and filter the finished item at the receiving warehouse from step 2.5Write downfinished item on-hand after; on-hand has increased by the production quantity over step 1.7. On the No path this only holds once Warehousing has finished the inbound procedure
Report the operation complete and confirm warehouse receipt: if something goes wrong
SymptomWhat to do
The order cannot be reported completedAn earlier operation is not completed, an operation is blocked, or an inspection order is still open
Report Orders Completed does not open after the last operationStop and record the operation's status and any message; this dialog's trigger condition is not documented
Quantity Delivered stays at 0 or finished-item on-hand does not increaseThe production receipt warehousing order may need manual processing, like Issue material to the job shop's issue order. Check Warehousing Orders (whinh2100m000) for an open receipt order before assuming an error

Variations

Variations
CaseWhat changes
Revision-controlled itemThe qualified training case must include the item revision as well as BOM and routing revisions
No routingOutside this basic foundation. The help states that no estimated production costs are defined when the order has no routing
More than one component
Task 3		Record and compare every expected component and estimated quantity in this task; issue every material line in Issue material to the job shop; the steps do not change
More than one operation
Task 3		Confirm every expected operation in routing sequence in this task; report each one complete in Report the operation complete and confirm warehouse receipt (step 6.4); the steps do not change
More than one component
Task 5		Record and compare every expected component and estimated quantity in Verify the generated foundation; issue every material line in this task; the steps do not change
Fully automatic material issue
Task 5		If Direct Initiate Inventory Issue and Direct Process Warehouse Order Line are both selected for the material, steps 5.4–5.9 complete themselves once the order is released; the steps do not change
More than one operation
Task 6		Confirm every expected operation in routing sequence in Verify the generated foundation; report each one complete in this task (step 6.4); the steps do not change
